strings.name: George Soros
strings.role: Investor · Founder of the Open Society Foundations
strings.summary: George Soros built his fortune in global macro investing and directed substantial resources to the Open Society Foundations, education and public affairs. A survivor of Nazi-occupied Hungary, he studied in London before entering finance in the United States. Both his investments and politically engaged philanthropy have international impact; the rating does not endorse his positions.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. The timeline ends with his 2025 honor and draws on biography updated in 2026. Philanthropy and political donations are distinct; the influence rating is not political endorsement.
strings.influence.rationale: Built influence in global macro investing and funded public affairs and education through the Open Society Foundations.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education or early career
strings.facts.fact-2.value: London School of Economics; influenced by Karl Popper
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Global macro investing
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Cross-market investments brought international influence; his sterling trade became a notable example.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: International philanthropic network
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Funded education, human rights and public affairs, and helped establish Central European University.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Presidential Medal of Freedom
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Received the US honor, accepted on his behalf by his son Alexander.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Foundation leadership transition
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Alexander Soros became chair of the Open Society Foundations board.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Expanded foundation funding
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Open Society announced his transfer of$18 billion to the foundations.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Sterling trade attracts attention
strings.timeline.event-4.text: His fund’s short position became prominent during Britain’s exit from the European exchange-rate mechanism.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Central European University opens
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Supported the university’s founding to advance international research and higher education.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Philanthropy begins
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Funded scholarships for Black South African students under apartheid.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Investment-management firm founded
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Established Soros Fund Management in the United States and developed hedge-fund operations.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Moves to London
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Studied at the London School of Economics; moved to the United States in 1956.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in Budapest
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Grew up in a Jewish family and survived the Nazi occupation as a teenager.
